body.translated_text: Determination of the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>)

body.text: sapakṣa eva sattvaṃ niścitamiti vartate / samānaḥ pakṣaḥ sapakṣaḥ / pakṣeṇa saha sadṛśo dṛṣṭāntadharmītyarthaḥ / sapakṣa eva satvaṃ niścitamityanvayasaṃjñakaṃ dvitīyaṃ rūpam / atra sattvagrahaṇena viruddhasya nirāsaḥ, yathā - śabdo nityaḥ kṛtakatvāt ghaṭavat / kṛtakatva hi nityatvavipakṣeṇānityatvena vyāptamiti viruddhamucyate / evakāreṇa sādhāraṇasya nirāsaḥ, yathā - nityaśśabdaḥ prameyatvāt ghaṭavat / prameyatvaṃ hi vikalpaviṣayīkṛtatvam, tacca sapakṣe ākāśādau vipakṣe ca ghaṭādau sarvatrāstīti sādhāraṇamucyate / sattvaśabdāt pūrvasminnevakāreṇa sarvasapakṣāvyāpino 'pi prayatnānantarīyakasya hetutvaṃ kathitam / yathā - anityaśśabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvādghaṭavadvidyudvat / niścitagrahaṇena sandigdhānvayasya nirāsaḥ, yathā - asarvajño 'yaṃ kaścit vaktṛtvādiṣṭapuru ṣavat / iṣṭapuruṣe sapakṣe ca vaktṛtvamasarvajñatvena vyāptamavyāptaṃ vā na jñāyate //
body.translated_text: "Ascertained presence in the positive example only" — this continues. The positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is that which has a similar thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). The meaning is: a subject of the example similar to the thesis. "Ascertained presence in the positive example only" — this is the second characteristic, designated as "positive concomitance" (<s>anvaya</s>). By the word "presence," the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) is rejected, as in: "Sound is permanent because it is produced, like a pot" — for being produced is pervaded by impermanence, the opposite of permanence, hence it is called contradictory. By the word "only," the common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) is rejected, as in: "Sound is permanent because it is knowable, like a pot" — for knowability, being the object of conceptual cognition, exists everywhere — in the positive example such as space and in the negative example such as a pot — hence it is called common. By the word "only" before "presence," the argument of one that does not pervade all positive examples (<s>sarvasapakṣāvyāpin</s>) is also declared to be a valid reason, as in: "Sound is impermanent because it is produced by effort, like a pot, like lightning." By the word "ascertained," the doubtfully concomitant (<s>sandigdhānvaya</s>) is rejected, as in: "This person is not omniscient because he speaks, like a desired person" — for in the positive example of the desired person, whether the property of speaking is pervaded by non-omniscience or not is not known.

body.text: vipakṣanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of the negative example (<s>vipakṣa</s>)

body.text: asapakṣe cāsattvameva niścitam / na sapakṣo 'sapakṣaḥ / tatrāsattvameva niścitaṃ vyatirekasaṃjñakaṃ tṛtīyaṃ rūpam / atrāpyasattvagrahaṇena viruddhasya nirāsaḥ / yathā nityaśśabdaḥ kṛtakatvādghaṭavat / viruddho hi vipakṣe 'sti / evakāreṇa sādhāraṇasya vipakṣaikadeśavṛtternirāsaḥ / prayatnānantarīyakatve sādhye anityatvaṃ vipakṣaikadeśe vidhudādāvasti / ākāśādau nāsti / tato niyamenāsya nirāsaḥ / asattvavacanātpūrvasminnavadhāraṇe ayamarthaḥ syāt / vipakṣa eva yo nāsti sa hetuḥ / tathā ca prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ sapakṣe 'pi nāsti, tato na hetuḥ syāt, tataḥ pūrva na kṛtamiti / niścitagrahaṇena sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikasya nirāsaḥ / yathāvītarāgo 'yaṃ puruṣo vaktṛtvāt, rathyāpuruṣavat / yatrāvītarāgatvaṃ nāsti tatra vaktṛtvamapi nāsti, yathopalakhaṇḍe / yadi nāma pāṣaṇakhaṇḍādubhayaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ tathāpi na jñāyate kimavītarāgatvanivṛttyā pāṣaṇakhaṇḍādbaktṛtvaṃ nivṛttaṃ, ahosvit svata eveti / tataḥ sandigdhavyatireko 'yamanaikāntikaḥ / asattvaśabdātpaścādevakāreṇa vipakṣaikadeśavṛtternirāsaḥ / yathā - prayatnānantarīyakaśśabdo 'nityatvāt / anityatvaṃ vipakṣādākāśānnivṛttaṃ, na vidyutaḥ / tato vipakṣaikadeśavṛttitvamasya //
body.translated_text: And in the dissimilar case (<s>asapakṣa</s>), definite absence alone is established. What is not the similar case is the dissimilar case. The definite absence therein, called <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), is the third characteristic. Here too, by the term 'absence,' the contradictory reason (<s>viruddha</s>) is excluded. For example: 'Sound is permanent, because of being produced—like a pot.' The contradictory reason is present in the dissimilar case. By the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), the reason that is partly present in the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣaikadeśavṛtti</s>), i.e., the common reason (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>), is excluded. When impermanence is the property to be proven, non-eternality exists in a part of the dissimilar case such as lightning, but not in space and the like. Therefore it is excluded by restriction. Without the word 'absence' in the previous qualifier, the meaning would be: whatever reason is absent only in the dissimilar case [is valid]. And then, 'being produced by effort' would be absent even in the similar case, so it would not be a valid reason—hence the previous [qualifier] was not made. By the word 'definite' (<s>niścita</s>), the reason whose exclusion from the dissimilar case is doubtful (<s>sandigdha-vipakṣa-vyāvṛttika</s>) is excluded. For example: 'This person is free from passion, because of being a speaker—like a person on the street.' Where there is no freedom from passion, speech too is absent, as in a stone slab. Even though both are excluded from a stone slab, it is not known whether speech is excluded from the stone slab because of the exclusion of freedom from passion, or by its own nature. Therefore this is a doubtful exclusion, which is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). By the word 'absence' later and by 'alone,' the reason partly present in the dissimilar case is excluded. For example: 'Sound is produced by effort, because of being impermanent.' Impermanence is excluded from the dissimilar case of space but not from lightning. Therefore this has partial presence in the dissimilar case.

body.text: trirūpaprayogasya prayojanam
body.translated_text: The purpose of the triple-characteristic application

body.text: nanu sapakṣa eva sattyamityukte sāmārthyādevāsapakṣe cāsattvamiti gamyate / tatkimarthamubhayorupādanamiti cet? vipakṣaniyamārthamiti pūrvavṛddhāḥ / te ca trividha eva vipakṣo bhavatīti manyante / sādhyābhāvamātraṃ, sādhyādanyaḥ, sādhyena saha viruddhaśca prayoganiyamārthamiti kecit / anvayaprayogo vyatirekaprayogo vā niyamavānekaḥ prayoktavyo na dvāvapīti / sādharmyavaidharmyaprayogasūcanārthamiti kecit /
body.translated_text: If one objects: when it is stated that [the reason] is present only in the similar case, its absence in the dissimilar case is understood by implication—so what is the purpose of stating both? The ancient authorities say it is for the purpose of restricting the dissimilar case. They hold that the dissimilar case is of three kinds only. Some say [the purpose is] to restrict the application regarding: the mere absence of the property to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>), what is other than the <s>sādhya</s>, and what is contrary to the <s>sādhya</s>. One application only—either the positive (<s>anvaya</s>) or the negative (<s>vyatireka</s>)—should be stated as the restrictive one, not both. Some say it is for indicating the application through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).

body.text: triliṅgabhedanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of the three types of logical marks (<s>liṅga</s>)

body.text: trirūpāṇi ca trīṇyeva liṅgāni / trīṇi rūpāṇi yeṣāṃ tāni trirūpāṇi trīṇyeva liṅgāni / kāryaṃ trirūpaṃ liṅgam / svābhāvastrirūpaṃ liṅgam / anupalabdhistrirūpaṃ liṅgam / sādhanaṃ jñāpakaṃ heturvyāpyaṃ ceti liṅgāparanāmāni /
body.translated_text: The logical marks possessing the three characteristics are only three. Those which have three characteristics are called 'possessing three characteristics'—there are only three such logical marks. The effect (<s>kārya</s>) is a triple-characteristic logical mark. The essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is a triple-characteristic logical mark. Non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is a triple-characteristic logical mark. Means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), and what is pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) are alternative names for a logical mark.

body.text: kāryahetunirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of the effect-based reason (<s>kārya-hetu</s>)

body.text: tatra kāryaṃ yathā - yatra dhūmastatrāgniryathā mahānase, dhūmaścātreti / vyāptipakṣadharmatāsaṃjñakaṃ dvayavayavameva sādhanavākyaṃ saugatānām / anye tu pratijñāhetudṛṣṭāntopanayanigamanaṃ ceti pañcāvayavaṃ sādhanavākyamāhuḥ / upanyāsaścedṛśaḥ - agniratra, dhūmāt, yatra dhūmastatrāgniryathā mahānase, tathā cāyaṃ, tasmādagniriti / etaccāyuktam / pratijñāvacanamātrātsambandharahitāt sādhyapratipatterayogāt / sambandhābhāvastu śabdārthayoḥ sambandhadūṣaṇe pratipāditatvānna punarucyate / pratijñāmantareṇa pañcapyantahetuprayogo 'pyayuktaḥ / hetuṃ vinopanayadṛṣṭāntāvapyayuktau / yatra pratijñaiva nāsti tatra pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanaṃ kuto bhaviṣyatīti sarvamāmūlaṃ viśīrṇam /
body.translated_text: An example of the effect-based reason: 'Where there is smoke, there is fire—as in a kitchen. And there is smoke here.' For the Buddhists, the probative statement consists of only two parts, known as the statement of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the statement of the property of the subject (<s>pakṣa-dharmatā</s>). Others, however, hold five members: thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).

body.text: kāryasambandhanirapaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of the connection of the effect-based reason

body.text: ayaṃ ca kāryaheturviṣayabhedena trividhaḥ / agnyādau sādhye dhūmādiḥ trividhapratyakṣānupalambhena niścetavyaḥ / cakṣurādau sādhye jñānaṃ kādācitkāryotpādānniścīyate / rūpādau sādhye rasādirekasāmagryadhīnatayā niścīyate, yathā mātuluṅgaphale rasādrūpānumānam / na rūpādrasānumānam / atra rūpe janayitavye pūrvakaṃ rūpamupādānam / rasastu sahakārikāraṇam / pūrvapuñjāduttarapuñjasyotpattau nyāya eṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: This effect-based reason is of three kinds according to the difference of objects. When fire and the like are to be proven, smoke and the like are to be ascertained through the threefold non-apprehension of perception. When the sense organ such as the eye is to be proven, cognition is ascertained from the occasional arising of the effect. When form and the like are to be proven, taste and the like are ascertained from the single aggregate [of causal conditions].

body.text: nanūpādānasahakārikāraṇayoranvayavyatirekānuvidhānasya kāryaṃ prati tulyatvātko bhedaḥ? ucyate, yadvikriyayā yanniṣpattirekasantāne tatkāryaṃ pratipūrvakamupādānam / yatsantānāntare viśeṣodayanimittaṃ tatsahakārikāraṇam / yathā śālyaṅkure janayitavye śālibījamupādānam, kṣitisalilādi tatra sahakāri / tadevaṃ kāryahetustadutpattisambandhād gamaka iti sthitam //
body.translated_text: If one objects: since the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and the cooperating cause (<s>sahakāri-kāraṇa</s>) are equal in their conformity to positive and negative concomitance with respect to the effect, what is the difference? It is said: that by whose transformation something is produced within a single continuum (<s>eka-santāna</s>) is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), which has the effect as its successor. That which, in another continuum, is the occasion for the arising of a special modification

body.text: svabhāvahetunirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of the nature-based reason (<s>svabhāva-hetu</s>)

body.text:
svabhāvo yathā - svabhāvaḥ svasattāmātrabhāvini sādhyadharme yo heturucyate sa tasya sādhyasya dharmasya svabhāvo boddhavyaḥ /
yathā- vṛkṣavyavahārayogyo 'yaṃ śiṃśapāvyavahārayogyatvāt / ayamiti puraḥ paridṛśyamānaḥ padārtho dharmī / śiṃśapāvyavahārayogyatvāditi hetuḥ / śiṃśapāvyavahārayogyatvāditi ko 'rthaḥ?
body.translated_text: The nature-based reason: 'nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>) means that which is called a reason with respect to a property to be proven that consists in the mere existence of its own being—that is to be understood as the nature of that property to be proven. For example: 'This is fit for the convention "tree" because it is fit for the convention "<s>śiṃśapā</s>" (rosewood).' 'This' refers to what is before

body.text: śākhāpatravarṇasaṃsthānaviśeṣavyavahārayogyatvādityarthaḥ / vṛkṣavyavahārayogyatvaṃ sādhyam / nanvekatve sādhyasādhanabhāvo na yuktaḥ, pratijñārthaikadeśatvāt? na / abhede 'pi kaścitpratipattā śiṃśapāvyavahāraṃ kṛtvā tatra vṛkṣavyavahāraṃ prāk kṛtamapi vyāmohāt kiñcidāropya punarna karoti / sa idāniṃ svabhāvahetunā vyavahāryate / tasmādetayoḥ paramārthata ekatve 'pi vikalpabuddhau vyāvṛttisamāśrayeṇa samutpannāyāṃ bhedena pratibhāsanāt sādhyasādhanatvaṃ na virudhyata iti //
body.translated_text: one—the meaning is: because it is fit for the convention of a particular configuration of branches, leaves, color, and shape. Fitness for the convention 'tree' is the property to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>). If one objects: if [reason and property to be proven] are identical, the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) is not proper, since the reason would be a part of the thesis—no, because even when there is no real difference, some cognizer understands '<s>śiṃśapā</s>'

body.text: anupalabdhihetunirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of the non-apprehension reason (<s>anupalabdhi-hetu</s>)

body.text: anupalabdhiryathā - nāstīha pradeśe ghaṭaḥ, upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdheḥ / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyeti dṛśyasyetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: An example of non-apprehension: 'There is no pot in this place, because of the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for apprehension.' 'What fulfills the conditions for apprehension' means: what is perceptible (<s>dṛśya</s>).

body.text: nanvasataḥ kathaṃ dṛśyatā? ekendriyajñānagrāhyo pradeśādāvupalabhyamāne yadi ghaṭaḥ syāt dṛśya eva bhavediti / upalambhapratyayāntarasākalyāt dṛśtayā sambhāvitaḥ, na tu dṛśya eva / tasyānupalabdheriti hetuḥ / sa caikajñānasaṃsargipadārthādekajñānasaṃsargipadārthopalambhādvā niścīyata iti tadubhayaṃ karmakartṛbhāvena paryudāsavṛttyā anupalabdhirucyate, na tu prasajyavṛttyā upalabdhinivṛttimātram / taddhi svayameva na kiñciditi kathaṃ sādhanaṃ syāt / nāpi pratiṣedhyādanyasya jñānamātram, rūpopalambhādapi nāraṅgarasaniṣedhaprasaṅgāt / tasmānniṣedhyādanyadviśiṣṭameva vastudvayaṃ pradeśaḥ pradeśajñānaṃ vānupalabdhiriti sthitam /
body.translated_text: If one asks: how can there be visibility of what does not exist? If a pot, being graspable by a single sense cognition, were to exist in a place and the like where it would be apprehended, it would indeed be visible. It is to be regarded as visible due to the completeness of the other conditions for apprehension—but not that it is actually visible. Because of the non-apprehension of that,

body.text: abhāvo 'sādhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is not to be proven

body.text:
ata evābhāvo na sādhyate / tasya ghaṭaviviktapradeśagrāhiṇā pratyakṣeṇaiva siddhatvāt / abhāvavyavahārastu mṛḍhaṃ prati anulambhena sādhyate /
tathā hi - kaścinmūḍho rajaḥprabhṛtiṣu sāṃkhyaprasiddheṣu guṇeṣvanupalambhena pravarttitābhāvabyavahāro 'pi punaḥ sarvaṃ sarvatrāstīti svasiddhāntābhyāsāt kvāpi pradeśādau ghaṭānupalambhe satyapi nābhāvavyavahāraṃ karotītyanupalambhena trividho vyavahāraḥ kāryate / tatra niḥ śaṅkagamanāgamanalakṣaṇaḥ kāyiko vyavahāraḥ / ghaṭo nāstīti vācikaḥ / īdṛśa eva antarjalpākāro mānasikaśceti / anupalabdhertādātmyatadutpattisambandhanirūpaṇam anupalambhasya karmadharmapakṣe sādhyena saha [sādṛśye] tādātmyalakṣaṇa eva sambandho boddhavyaḥ / kartṛdharmapakṣe tu tadutpattiḥ /
tathā hi - ghaṭaviviktapradeśaḥ pradeśajñānaṃ vānupalabdhirityuktam / asadvyavahārayogyatvaṃ ca tasya svabhāvaḥ [na kārya] jñānaṃ tu pradeśasya kāryamiti //
body.translated_text: For this very reason, absence is not [independently] proven, since it is already established by perception itself which grasps the place as devoid of the pot. The conventional usage of absence, however, is proven to the confused person through non-apprehension. For example: some confused person, regarding <s>rajas</s> and other [qualities] well-known in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system,

body.text: anupalabdhervyapadeśaḥ
body.translated_text: The designation of non-apprehension

body.text:
nanu yadyanupalabdherapi tādātmyatadutpattī eva sambandhau, kathaṃ tarhi kāryasvabhāvābhyāmanupalabdherbhedaḥ? pratiṣedhasādhanāt bhedau na vastutaḥ /
yathoktamācāryeṇa - atra dvau vastusādhanau, ekaḥ pratiṣedhahetuḥ iti / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatvaviśiṣṭena deśavipakṛṣṭe sumervādau kālaviprakṛṣṭe bhaviṣyacchaṅkhacakravartyādau svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭe piśācādāvanupalambhamātrasambhave 'pi nābhāvavyavahāra ityuktaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Objection: If the relations of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) too are only identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>), then how does non-apprehension differ from [inferences based on] effect and essential nature? [Reply:] The difference is because it is a means of proving negation (<s>pratiṣedhasādhana</s>), not a real [ontological] difference. As the <s>Ācārya</s> (<s>Dharmakīrti</s>) has said: 'Here there are two [types of] proofs of real entities, and one negative proof.' Even though mere non-apprehension is possible in the case of [objects that are] spatially remote like <s>Sumeru</s>, etc., temporally remote like future universal monarchs with conch and wheel, etc., and remote in nature like demons, etc. — provided they satisfy the conditions for perceptibility (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatva</s>) — there is no conventional usage of absence. This is what is stated.

body.text: anupalabdhervartamānakāle anāgatakāle ca pramāṇam
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) as <s>pramāṇa</s> in the present and future times

body.text: iyaṃ cānupalabdhirvartamānakāle pramāṇaṃ viśiṣṭasmaraṇasadbhāve 'tītakāle ca, anāgatakāletvanupalabdhiḥ svayameva sandigdharūpā / tato na pramāṇam / [anayānulabdhyābhāvavyahāraḥ sādhyate, na tvabhāvaḥ / tasya pratyakṣeṇaiva siddhatvādityuktaṃ prāk] yathāhanyāyavādī -
body.translated_text: And this non-apprehension is a <s>pramāṇa</s> in the present time, and in the past time when the appropriate recollection exists. In the future time, however, non-apprehension is itself of doubtful nature. Therefore it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> [for the future]. [By this non-apprehension, the conventional usage of absence is established, but not absence itself — since that is established by <s>pratyakṣa</s> alone, as was stated earlier.] As the follower of the correct doctrine has said —

body.text:
amūḍhasmṛtisaṃskārasyātītasya vartamānasya ca pratipattṛpratyakṣasya
nivṛttiranupalabdhi rabhāvavyavahārasādhanī iti /
body.translated_text: 'For one of unconfused memory and impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the cessation — with respect to what is past and present — of the perceiver's direct perception is non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), which establishes the conventional usage of absence.'

body.text: anupalabdhibhedāḥ
body.translated_text: Types of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhibheda</s>)

body.text:
tatra yadā dūratvānniṣedhyasyāyogyadeśatvaṃ syāt, tadā dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ sākṣātprayoktuṃ na śakyata iti kāryānupalabdhyādayaḥ prayujyante / ata eveyaṃ prayogabhedena ṣoḍaśadhā bhavati /
(1) tatra svabhāvānupalabdhiryathā - nāstyatra dhūmaḥ, upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdheḥ / pratiṣedhyasya dhūmasya yaḥ svabhāvaḥ tasyehānupalabdhiḥ / (2) kāryānupalabdhiryathā - nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni dhūmakāraṇāni santi, dhūmābhāvāt / pratiṣedhyānāṃ hi dhūmakāraṇānāṃ kārya dhūmaḥ, tasyehānupalabdhiḥ / (3) kāraṇānupalabdhiryathā - nāstyatra dhūmaḥ dahanābhāvāt / pratiṣedhyasya dhūmasya kāraṇaṃ dahanaḥ, tasyehānupalabdhiḥ / (4) vyāpakānupalabdhiryathā - nātra śiṃśapā, vṛkṣābhāvāt / pratiṣedhyāyāḥ śiṃpāyāḥ vyāpako vṛkṣaḥ, tāsyehānupalabdhiḥ / (5) svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhiryathā - nātra śītasparśaḥ, vahneriti / pratiṣedhyasy śītasparśasya yaḥ svabhāvaḥ tasya viruddho vahniḥ tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (6) kāryaviruddhopalabdhiryathā - nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṇāni santi, vahneriti / antyadaśāprāptameva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ janayati, na sarvaṃ kāraṇām, tato viśeṣaṇopādānam / pratiṣedhyānāṃ śītakāraṇānāṃ kāryaṃ śītaṃ, tasya viruddho vahniḥ, tasyehopalabdhiḥ / (7) kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhiryathā - nāsya romaharṣādiviśeṣāḥ santi, sannihitadahanaviśeṣatvāt / pratiṣedhyānāṃ romaharṣādiviśeṣāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ śīta, tasya viruddho dahanaviśeṣaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (8) vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiryathā - nātra tuṣārasparśaḥ, dahanāt / pratiṣedhyasya tuṣārasparśasya vyāpakaṃ śītaṃ, tasya viruddho dahanaviśeṣaḥ tasyehopalabdhiḥ / (9) svabhāvaviruddhakāryopalabdhiryathā, nātra śītasparśaḥ, dhūmāt / pratiṣedhyasya śītasparśasya yaḥ svabhāvastasya viruddho 'gniḥ, tasya kārya dhūmaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (10) kāryaviruddhakāryopalabdhiryathā - nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṃṇāni santi dhūmāditi / pratiṣedhyānāṃ śītakāraṇānāṃ kāryaṃ śītaṃ, tasya viruddho vahniḥ, tasya kāryaṃ dhūmaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (11) kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhiryathā - na romaharṣādiviśeṣayukta sparśavānayaṃ pradeśo dhūmāditi / pratiṣedhyānāṃ hi romaharṣādisparśaviśeṣāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ śītam, tasya viruddho 'gniḥ, tasya kāryaṃ dhūmaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (12) vyāpakaviruddhakāryopalabdhiryathā - nātra tuṣārasparśaḥ, dhūmāditi / niṣedhyasya tuṣārasparśasya vyāpakaṃ śītam, tasya viruddho 'gniḥ, tasya kāryaṃ dhūmaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (13) svabhāvaviruddhavyāptopalabdhiryathā - nātra vahniḥ, tuṣārasparśāt / pratiṣedhyasya hi vahneryaḥ svabhāvastasya viruddhaṃ śītam, tena vyāptastuṣārasparśaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (14) kāryaviruddhavyāptopalabdhiryathā - nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni vahnikāraṇāni santi, tuṣārasparśāditi / pratiṣedhyānāṃ vahnikāraṇānāṃ kāryaṃ vahniḥ, tasya viruddhaṃ śītam, tena vyāptastuṣārasparśaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (15) kāraṇaviruddhavyāptopalabdhiryathā - nātra dhūmastuṣārasparśāditi / pratiṣedhyasya dhūmasya yatkāraṇamagniḥ, tasya viruddhaṃ śītam, tena vyāptastuṣārasparśaḥ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / (16) vyāpakaviruddhavyāptopalabdhiryathā - nāyaṃ nityaḥ, kadācitkāryakāritvāt / pratiṣedhyasya nityatvasya niratiśayatvaṃ vyāpakaṃ, tasya viruddhaṃ sātiśayatvaṃ, tena vyāptaṃ kadācitkāryakāritvaṃ, tasya cehopalabdhiḥ / ete ca kāryānupalabdhyādayaḥ pañcadaśa prayogāḥ svabhāvānupalabdhisvabhāvā eva pratipattavyāḥ / prayuktibhedena paraṃ bhedaḥ / tatra svabhāvānupalambhenāsad vyavahārayogyatvaṃ sādhyate, na tvābhāvaḥ / tasya ca pratyakṣeṇaiva siddhatvāt / aparaiśca sarvairabhāvo 'bhāvabyavahāraśca sādhyate, teṣāṃ parokṣaviṣayatvāt //
body.translated_text:
There, when the thing to be negated is in an unfit location due to remoteness, direct non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) cannot be directly employed — therefore non-apprehension of the effect, etc. are employed. For this reason, it becomes sixteenfold through differences in application.
(1) Non-apprehension of the essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no smoke here, because of the non-apprehension of what satisfies the conditions for perceptibility.' The essential nature of the negated smoke is not apprehended here.
(2) Non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There are no unobstructed causes of smoke here, because of the absence of smoke.' For smoke is the effect of the negated smoke-causes, and that [smoke] is not apprehended here.
(3) Non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no smoke here, because of the absence of fire.' Fire is the cause of the negated smoke, and that [fire] is not apprehended here.
(4) Non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the absence of trees.' Tree is the pervader of the negated <s>śiṃśapā</s>, and that [tree] is not apprehended here.
(5) Apprehension of what is incompatible with the essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no cold sensation here, because of fire.' Fire is incompatible with the essential nature of the negated cold sensation, and that [fire] is apprehended here.
(6) Apprehension of what is incompatible with the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There are no unobstructed causes of cold here, because of fire.' Only a cause that has reached its final stage produces an effect, not every cause — hence the qualifier [unobstructed]. Cold is the effect of the negated cold-causes; fire is incompatible with that [cold]; and that [fire] is apprehended here.
(7) Apprehension of what is incompatible with the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There are no special features such as goosebumps here, because of the presence of a particular fire.' Cold is the cause of the negated goosebumps, etc.; a particular fire is incompatible with that [cold]; and that [fire] is apprehended here.
(8) Apprehension of what is incompatible with the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no frost-sensation here, because of fire.' Cold is the pervader of the negated frost-sensation; a particular fire is incompatible with that [cold]; and that [fire] is apprehended here.
(9) Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible with the essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no cold sensation here, because of smoke.' Fire is incompatible with the essential nature of the negated cold sensation; smoke is the effect of that [fire]; and that [smoke] is apprehended here.
(10) Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible with the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There are no unobstructed causes of cold here, because of smoke, etc.' Cold is the effect of the negated cold-causes; fire is incompatible with that [cold]; smoke is the effect of that [fire]; and that [smoke] is apprehended here.
(11) Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible with the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'This region does not have a touch possessing goosebumps and similar features, because of smoke.' Cold is the cause of the negated goosebumps, etc.; fire is incompatible with that [cold]; smoke is the effect of that [fire]; and that [smoke] is apprehended here.
(12) Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible with the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no frost-sensation here, because of smoke.' Cold is the pervader of the negated frost-sensation; fire is incompatible with that [cold]; smoke is the effect of that [fire]; and that [smoke] is apprehended here.
(13) Apprehension of what is pervaded by the incompatible of the essential nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no fire here, because of frost-sensation.' Cold is incompatible with the essential nature of the negated fire; frost-sensation is pervaded by that [cold]; and that [frost-sensation] is apprehended here.
(14) Apprehension of what is pervaded by the incompatible of the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There are no unobstructed causes of fire here, because of frost-sensation.' Fire is the effect of the negated fire-causes; cold is incompatible with that [fire]; frost-sensation is pervaded by that [cold]; and that [frost-sensation] is apprehended here.
(15) Apprehension of what is pervaded by the incompatible of the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'There is no smoke here, because of frost-sensation.' Fire is the cause of the negated smoke; cold is incompatible with that [fire]; frost-sensation is pervaded by that [cold]; and that [frost-sensation] is apprehended here.
(16) Apprehension of what is pervaded by the incompatible of the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>): e.g., 'This is not permanent, because of occasionally producing effects.' Unlimitedness (<s>niratiśayatva</s>) is the pervader of the negated permanence; having degrees (<s>sātiśayatva</s>) is incompatible with that [unlimitedness]; occasional effect-production is pervaded by that [having degrees]; and that [occasional effect-production] is apprehended here.
These fifteen applications beginning with non-apprehension of the effect are to be understood as essentially being of the nature of non-apprehension of the essential nature. The difference is merely in application. Among these, by non-apprehension of the essential nature, fitness for the conventional usage of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>) is established, but not absence [itself] — since that is established by <s>pratyakṣa</s> alone. By all the others, however, both absence and the conventional usage of absence are established, since they have imperceptible objects.

body.text: iti tarkabhāṣāyāṃ svārthānumānaparicchedo dvitīyaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, on inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>), in the <s>Tarkabhāṣā</s>.

body.text: parārthānumānam
body.translated_text: Inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>)

body.text: parārthānumānalakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: Definition of inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>)

body.text: trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārthānumānam / anvayavyatirekapakṣadharmatāsaṃjñakāni trīṇi rūpāṇi, yena vacanena prakhyāpyante tadvacanamupacārādanumānaśabdenocyate //
body.translated_text: The statement of the triple-characterized mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>) is inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). The three characteristics called positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), and being a property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) — the verbal statement by which these are proclaimed is called <s>anumāna</s> by figurative extension.

body.text: tasya dvaividhyam
body.translated_text: Its twofold nature

body.text: tad dvividham sādharmyavadvaidharmyavacca / sādhyadharmidṛṣṭāntadhamiṇorhetu sattākṛtaṃ sādṛśyaṃ sādharmyam / tadyasyāsti tat sādharmyavat sādhanavākyam / sādhyadharmidṛṣṭāntadharmiṇorhetusattākṛtaṃ vaisādṛśyaṃ vaidharmyam / tadyasyāsti tadvaidharmyavata sādhanavākyam /
body.translated_text: That is twofold: based on similarity (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) and based on dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>). The similarity produced by the presence of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) in both the subject to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) and the example (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>) is <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity). A probative statement that possesses that is a statement based on similarity. The dissimilarity produced by the [respective] presence and absence of the <s>hetu</s> in the subject and the example is <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity). A probative statement that possesses that is a statement based on dissimilarity.

body.text: svabhāvahetossādharmyavatprayoganirūpaṇam, saṃskṛtasya sarvasya kṣaṇika tvasamarthanaṃ ca tatra svabhāvahetoḥ sādharmyavantaṃ prayogaṃ darśayituṃ sautrāntikamatamāśritya bhagavatā yaduktaṃ -
body.translated_text:
Demonstration of the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) through the statement based on similarity, and the proof of the momentariness of all conditioned things.
To demonstrate the application of the essential-nature reason through a statement based on similarity, relying on the <s>Sautrāntika</s> doctrine, the Blessed One stated —

body.text: `saṃskṛtaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ sarvaṃ' iti /
body.translated_text: 'All that is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>).'

body.text: tad vyutpādyate / sametya sambhūya hetupratyayaiḥ kṛtaṃ vastujātaṃ saṃskṛtam / kṣaṇikamiti utpattikṣaṇa eva sattvāt / sarvasaṃkṛtavināśanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: This is explained. 'Conditioned' (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) means: a real entity (<s>vastujāta</s>) produced by coming together of causes and conditions (<s>hetupratyaya</s>). 'Momentary' (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) means: because it exists only at the moment of arising. // Demonstration of the destruction of all conditioned things

body.text: `sarvaṃ tāvat ghaṭādikaṃ vastu mudgarādisannidhau nāśaṃ gacchat dṛśyate / tatra yena svarūpeṇa antyāvasthāyāṃ ghaṭādikaṃ vinaśyati taccet svarūpamutpannamātrasya vidyate tadānīmutpādānantarameva tena vinaṣṭavyamiti vyaktamasya kṣaṇikatvam /'
body.translated_text: 'All things such as pots, etc. are observed to perish in the presence of a hammer, etc. Now, if the very form in which the pot, etc. perishes in its final stage already existed in [the pot] at the moment of its arising, then it should have perished immediately after arising — thus its momentariness is evident.'

body.text: athedṛśa eva svabhāvastasya svahetorjātaḥ, yat kiyantaṃ kālaṃ sthitvā vinaśyatīti /
body.translated_text: But suppose this very nature of it was born from its own cause, such that it persists for some time and then perishes?

body.text: `evaṃ tarhi mudgarādisannidhāne ca eṣa eva asya svabhava iti punarapyanena tāvantameva kālaṃ sthātavyam, punarapyevamiti naiva vinaśyediti / tasmāt kṣaṇadvayasthāyitvenāpyutpattau prathamakṣaṇavad dvitīyakṣaṇe 'pi kṣaṇadvayasthāyitvāt punaraparaṃ kṣaṇadvayamavatiṣṭheta / evaṃ tṛtīye 'pi kṣaṇe tatsvabhāvatvānnaiva vinaśyatīti /'
body.translated_text: 'If so, then even in the presence of a hammer, etc., this would be its very nature — and therefore it should persist for exactly the same duration again, and again in the same way, and thus it would never perish. Therefore, even if assumed to persist for two moments, since at the moment of arising it would persist for two moments just as in the first moment, it would then persist for yet another two moments in the second moment. Likewise in the third moment, since it would be of the same nature, it would never perish.'

body.text: syādetat, sthāvarameva tadvastu svahetorjātam, balena virodhakena mudgarādinā vināśyata iti? tadasat, kathaṃ punaretadyujyate, na ca tadvinaśyati sthāvaratvāt, vināśaśca tasya virodhina balena kriyata iti? na hyetatsambhavati jīvati devadatto maraṇaṃ cāsya bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: One might say: that very thing, having arisen from its own cause, is stable, and is destroyed by a forceful opposing agent, such as a hammer and the like. That is wrong. For how is this consistent — that it does not perish because it is stable, and yet its destruction is brought about by the force of an opposing agent? For it is not possible that <s>Devadatta</s> is alive and yet his death also occurs.

body.text: atha vinaśyati, kathaṃ tarhyavinaśvaraṃ tadvastu svahetorjātam? na hi mriyate cāmaraṇadharmā ceti yujyate vaktum / tasmādanaśvaratve kadācidapi naśāyogāt, dṛṣṭatvācca nāśasya, naśvarameva tadvastu svahetorupajāta ityaṅgīkurmaḥ / tasmādutpannamātrameva vinaśyati / tatha ca kṣaṇakṣayitvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati / prayogaḥ punarevaṃ kartavyaḥ - yadyat vinaśvarasvarūpaṃ tattadanantarānavasthāyi yathā antyakṣaṇavartighaṭasya svarūpam / vinaśvararūpaṃ ca rūpādikamudayakāla iti svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: But if it does perish, how then is that thing imperishable, having arisen from its own cause? For it is not consistent to say: 'it dies and yet is of an undying nature.' Therefore, if it were imperishable, destruction could never occur; and since destruction is observed, we accept that that very thing, having arisen from its own cause, is indeed perishable. Therefore, it perishes at the very moment of arising. And thus momentariness (<s>kṣaṇakṣayitva</s>) is established. The formal argument should be constructed thus: Whatever has a perishable nature is not enduring in the immediately subsequent moment, like the nature of a pot at its final moment. And form and the like are of perishable nature at the moment of arising — this is the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-based reason).

body.text: nirviśeṣaṇasvabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ
body.translated_text: The Argument of the Unqualified <s>Svabhāvahetu</s> (Nature-Based Reason)

body.text: yadi kṣaṇakṣayiṇo bhāvāḥ, kathaṃ tarhi sa evāyamiti pratyabhijñānaṃ syāt? ucyate -
body.translated_text: If things perish at every moment, how then can there be recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) in the form 'this is the very same [thing]'? We reply:

body.text: nirantarasadṛśāparāparotpādādavidyānubandhācca pūrvakṣaṇavināśakāla eva tatsadṛśaṃ kṣaṇāntaramudayate / tenākāreṇa vailakṣaṇyasyābhāvād bhāvena cāvyavadhānāt bhede 'pi sa evāyamityabhedādhyavasāyapratyayaḥ pṛthagjanānāṃ prasūyate / atyantabhinneṣvapi ca lūnapunarjātakuśakeśādiṣvapi dṛṣṭa eva sa evāyamiti pratyayaḥ / tathehāpi kiṃ na sambhāvyate? tasmātsarva saṃskṛtaṃ kṣaṇikamiti siddhamevaitat nirviśeṣaṇasya svabhāvahetorayaṃ prayoga iti // tathāparo 'pi nirviśeṣaṇaprayogaḥ - yatsat tatsarvamanityaṃ, yathā ghaṭaḥ / santaścāmī pramāṇapratītāḥ / tathāparo 'pi vedasya pauruṣayatvasādhanāya svabhāvahetuḥ / yadvākyaṃ tatpauruṣeyaṃ, yathā rathyāpuruṣa vākyam / vākyaṃ cedam -
body.translated_text: Because of the uninterrupted arising of successive similar [moments], and because of the connection with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), at the very moment when the preceding moment perishes, another moment similar to it arises. Since there is no difference in appearance by that form, and since there is no interruption in existence, even though [things are] different, the cognition of non-difference arises in ordinary persons as 'this is the very same [thing].' And even in cases of things that are utterly different, such as cut-and-regrown <s>kuśa</s> grass, hair, and the like, the cognition 'this is the very same' is directly observed. Why should it not be possible here as well? Therefore, all that is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is momentary — this is indeed established. This is the argument of the unqualified <s>svabhāvahetu</s>. And thus another unqualified argument [can be stated]: Whatever is real (<s>sat</s>), all that is impermanent, like a pot. And these [things under consideration] are real, as apprehended by valid means of knowledge. And yet another <s>svabhāvahetu</s> for establishing the human origin of the <s>Vedas</s>: Whatever is a sentence is of human origin, like the sentence of a person in the street. And this is a sentence —

body.text: `agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāma' iti /
body.translated_text: 'One who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>.'

body.text: saviśeṣaṇasvabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ
body.translated_text: The Argument of the Qualified <s>Svabhāvahetu</s>

body.text: saviśeṣaṇaprayogo yathā - yadyadutpattimat tatsarvamanityaṃ, yathā ghaṭaḥ / utpattimāṃśca śabdaḥ / anutpannebhyo vyāvṛtto bhāva utpanna ucyate / yadā saiva vyāvṛttirvyāvṛttyantaravyavacchedena vyatiriktocyate bhāvasyotpattiriti tadā kalpitena bhedena svabhāvabhūtadharmeṇa viśiṣṭaḥ svabhāvo hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: An argument with a qualification is, for example: Whatever has origination, all that is impermanent, like a pot. And sound has origination. A thing that is excluded from non-originated things is called 'originated.' When that very exclusion, being demarcated from other exclusions, is called distinct from the thing, [then] 'the thing's origination' — with a conceptually constructed distinction, the nature-based reason qualified by a property that is of the nature [of the subject] is [called] a qualified <s>svabhāvahetu</s>.

body.text: bhinnaviśeṣaṇasvabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ
body.translated_text: The Argument of the <s>Svabhāvahetu</s> with a Distinct Qualifier

body.text: tathā bhinnaviśeṣaṇasya prayogaḥ - yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ, kṛtakaśca śabdaḥ / nanu citraguriti bhinnaviśeṣaṇasya prayogaḥ, yathā cātra citragośabde bhinnaviśeṣaṇavācako 'sti na tathā kṛtakaśabde bhinnaviśeṣaṇavācakaṃ kimapyasti / tatkathaṃ bhinnaviśeṣaṇasyodāharaṇamiti ced? ucyate - apekṣitaparavyāpāro hi svabhāvaniṣpattau bhāvaḥ kṛtakaḥ ityucyate / tatraḥ kṛtakaśabdaḥ paravyāpārasāpekṣaṃ svabhābaṃ prakṛtyaiva vadan bhinnaviśeṣaṇamevāha //
body.translated_text: The argument of one with a distinct qualifier is as follows: Whatever is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is impermanent, like a pot. And sound is produced. Now, [one might object:] '<s>citragu</s>' (spotted cow) is an example of [a word with] a distinct qualifier, and just as in the word '<s>citragu</s>' there is an element denoting a distinct qualifier, there is no such element in the word '<s>kṛtaka</s>' denoting a distinct qualifier. So how is this an example of a distinct qualifier? We reply: A thing that requires the activity of another for the accomplishment of its own nature is called '<s>kṛtaka</s>' (produced). There, the word '<s>kṛtaka</s>,' by its very root expressing a nature dependent on the activity of another, does indeed express a distinct qualifier.

body.text: prayuktabhinnaviśeṣaṇasvabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ
body.translated_text: The Argument of the <s>Svabhāvahetu</s> with an Applied Distinct Qualifier

body.text: prayuktabhinnaviśeṣaṇasya svabhāvasya prayogaḥ - yaḥ pratyayabhedabhedī sa kṛtakaḥ, yathā dhūmaḥ, pratyayabhedabhedī ca śabdaḥ / pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ, tasya bhedastena bhettuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa pratyayabhedabhedī / kāraṇamahattvena mahattvaṃ kāraṇālpatvenālpatvaṃ yasyetyarthaḥ pratyayabhedabhediśabdasya bhinnaviśeṣaṇavācakasyātra prayuktatvāt prayuktabhinnaviśeṣaṇo 'yam / svabhāvahetoḥ nānāprabhedadarśanaṃ ca vyāmohanivṛttaye dharmabhedakalpanayāpi svabhāvahetureva prayujyata iti pratipādayitum /
body.translated_text: The argument of the nature-based reason with an applied distinct qualifier is: That which varies with variation of conditions is produced, like smoke. And sound varies with variation of conditions. A 'condition' (<s>pratyaya</s>) is a cause; 'to vary with its variation' means having the character of varying with it — [meaning:] through greatness of cause there is greatness, through smallness of cause there is smallness. Since the word '<s>pratyayabhedabhedin</s>' (varying with variation of conditions), which denotes a distinct qualifier, is used here, this is [called a <s>svabhāvahetu</s>] with an applied distinct qualifier. The demonstration of the various sub-types of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is for the purpose of removing confusion, to show that even through the conceptual construction of property-distinctions, it is the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> alone that is employed.

body.text: svabhāvahetorvaidharmyavatprayoganirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of the Dissimilar-Instance Argument of the <s>Svabhāvahetu</s>

body.text: svabhāvahetorvaidharmyavān prayogo yathā - yadyadānantarānavasthāyi na bhavati na tattadā vinaśvararūpaṃ, yathākāśam / vinaśvararūpaṃ ca rūpādikamudayakāle / vyatirekaprayoge sādhanābhāvena sādhyābhāvasya vyāptatvāt sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanābhāve niyato bhavatīti boddhavyam / tathāparo 'pi vaidharmyavān prayogaḥ - yatra kṣaṇikatvaṃ nāsti tatra sattvamapi nāsti, yathā gaganāravinde / saṃśca śabdaḥ / tathā yatrānityatvaṃ nivṛttaṃ tatrotpattimattvamapi, yathā kūrmaromṇi / utpattimāṃśca śabdaḥ / yatrānityatvaṃ nivṛttaṃ tatra kṛtakamapi, yathā śaśaśriṅge / kṛtakaśca śabdaḥ / yatra kṛtakatvaṃ nāsti tatra pratyayabhedabheditvamapi nāsti, yathā gagane / pratyayabhedabhedī ca śabda iti //
body.translated_text: The dissimilar-instance argument of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is as follows: Whatever is not enduring in the immediately subsequent moment, that is not of a perishable nature, like space. And form and the like are of perishable nature at the moment of arising. In the negative argument, it should be understood that the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) — that is, the absence of the probandum is invariably [present] in the absence of the probans. And thus another dissimilar-instance argument: Where momentariness does not exist, there existence (<s>sattva</s>) also does not exist, like a sky-lotus. And sound exists. Likewise: Where impermanence is absent, there origination is also [absent], like in tortoise-hair. And sound has origination. Where impermanence is absent, there being-produced is also [absent], like in a hare's horn. And sound is produced. Where being-produced does not exist, there varying-with-conditions also does not exist, like in space. And sound varies with conditions.

body.text: kāryahetoḥ sādharmyavadvaidharmyavatprayoganirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of the Similar and Dissimilar Arguments of the <s>Kāryahetu</s> (Effect-Based Reason)

body.text: kāryahetoḥ sādharmyavān prayogo yathā - yatra yatra dhūmastatra tatrāgniḥ, yathā mahānase, dhūmaścātra / kāryaheturapi pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ siddha eva kāryakāraṇabhāve sati kāraṇe sādhye prayoktavyaḥ / vaidharmyaprayogo yathā asatyagnau na bhavatyeva dhūmaḥ yathā - mahāhrade / asti ceha dhūma iti /
body.translated_text: The similar-instance argument of the <s>kāryahetu</s> is as follows: Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen. And there is smoke here. The <s>kāryahetu</s> too, when the cause-effect relation is established through perception and non-apprehension, should be employed when a cause is the probandum. The dissimilar-instance argument is as follows: In the absence of fire, there is certainly no smoke, as in a great lake. And there is smoke here.

body.text: anupalabdhessādharmyavad prayogaḥ
body.translated_text: The Similar-Instance Argument of Non-Apprehension (<s>Anupalabdhi</s>)

body.text: anupalabdheḥ sādharmyavan prayogo 'vayavinirākaraṇāya yathā - yadyatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sannopalabhyate tattatrāsadvyavahārayogyam, yathā naraśirasi śṛṅgam / nopalabhyate cātropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaḥ parābhimato 'vayavī ghaṭaśabdavācyeṣu kapāleṣu /
body.translated_text: The similar-instance argument of non-apprehension, for the purpose of refuting the whole (<s>avayavin</s>), is as follows: Whatever fulfills the conditions for being apprehended, yet is not apprehended when existing, that is fit to be conventionally treated as non-existent there, like a horn on a man's head. And the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) as maintained by the opponent, denoted by the word 'pot,' is not apprehended though fulfilling the conditions for apprehension in the potsherds.

body.text: vaidharmyavatprayoganirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of the Dissimilar-Instance Argument

body.text: anupalabdhervaidharmyavān prayogo yathā - yatsadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ tadupalabhyata eva, yathā nīlādiviśeṣaḥ / neha upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya sata upalabdhirghaṭasyeti /
body.translated_text: The dissimilar-instance argument of non-apprehension is as follows: Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions for apprehension is indeed apprehended, like a particular shade of blue and the like. But here there is no apprehension of the existing pot that fulfills the conditions for apprehension.

body.text: sādhyasādhanayorvyāptiḥ
body.translated_text: Pervasion (<s>Vyāpti</s>) of the Probandum and the Probans

body.text: sarvatra sādharmyavati sādhanavākye sādhyena sādhanaṃ vyāptam / baidharmyavati [punaḥ] sādhanavākye sādhanābhāvena sādhyābhāvo vyāpta iti pratipattavyam / sādhanasya ca sādhye
body.translated_text: In every similar-instance probative statement, the probans is pervaded by the probandum. In the dissimilar-instance probative statement, the absence of the probandum is pervaded by the absence of the probans — this should be understood. The statement of the invariable relation of the probans to the probandum,

body.text: niyatatvakathanaṃ sādhyābhāvasya sādhanābhāve niyatatvakathanaṃ nāma vyāptirabhidhīyate / tataḥ pramāṇena vyāptisiddhau satyāṃ nedaṃ kvāpi śaṅkanīyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca syāta, sādhyaṃ ca tatra dharmiṇi na syāditi / parāṅgīkṛteśvarasādhakānumānasya nirasanam
body.translated_text: [or equivalently,] the statement of the invariable relation of the absence of the probandum to the absence of the probans, is called <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). Therefore, when pervasion is established through valid means of knowledge with complete enumeration, there is no room for the doubt: 'the probans may be present, yet the probandum may not be present in that subject.' Refutation of the Inference Accepted by the Opponent as Proving God (<s>Īśvara</s>)

body.text: yatra pramāṇena sarvopasaṃhāravatī vyāptireva na siddhā, tatra śaṅkāprasaro 'nivāryaḥ / yatheśvarasiddhau kāryatvānumāne / tathā hi teṣāṃ sādhanopanyāsaḥ / ihānyaḥ sarvajño bhagavān bhavatu vā mā bhūt, īśvaraḥ punassarvajñaḥ śakyate sādhayitum / tathā hi, loke trayaḥ khalu bhāvāḥ kecinniścitakartṛkāḥ, yathā ghaṭādayaḥ / kecinniścitakartṛnivṛttayaḥ, yathā vyomādayaḥ / anye punaḥ sandigdhakartṛkāḥ, yathā kṣityādayaḥ / na punaretebhyo 'nyaḥ prakāro 'sti / tatra ye dṛśyamānotpattayo vanaspatyādayo ye ca cirotpannā viśvambharādayaḥ te sarve sandigdhakartṛtvena vyavatiṣṭhamānā buddhimatkartṛkāḥ kāryatvāt, ghaṭādivat / nāyamasiddho hetuḥ, kāryatvasya sarvoṣāṃ pramāṇasiddhatvāt / nāpi viruddhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt / na cānaikāntaḥ, sādhyaviparyaye bādhakapramāṇasadbhāvāt / tathāhi - kārya tāvat buddhimataḥ kumbhakārādupajāyamānaṃ bhūyodarśanasahāyena mānasa pratyakṣeṇopalabdham /
body.translated_text: Where pervasion with complete enumeration is not at all established through valid means of knowledge, there the scope of doubt is irresistible. As in the inference from being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) for the proof of God (<s>Īśvara</s>). For their presentation of the probans is as follows: 'Let there be or not be any other omniscient Blessed One here — [the existence of] God who is omniscient can nonetheless be proven. For, in the world, there are indeed three [kinds of] things: some whose maker is ascertained, like pots and the like; some whose maker is ascertainably absent, like space and the like; and others whose maker is in doubt, like the earth and the like. There is no other category beyond these. Among these, trees and the like whose origination is observed, and the earth and the like which originated long ago — all these, standing as things whose maker is doubtful, have an intelligent maker, because they are effects, like pots and the like. This is not an unestablished reason, because the effectness of all [these things] is established by valid means of knowledge. Nor is it a contradictory [reason], because it is present in a similar instance. Nor is it inconclusive, because there is a blocking valid cognition against the opposite of the probandum. For an effect, to begin with, is observed through mental perception aided by repeated observation to arise from an intelligent [being] such as a potter.

body.text: tadyadi buddhimantareṇāpi syāt tadānīṃ buddhimataḥ sakāśātkadācidapi nopajāyeta / kāraṇābhāve kāryasya sakṛdapyutpādāyogāt / tasmānnedaṃ kvāpi śaṅkanīyaṃ kāryaṃ ca syāt na buddhimaddhetukamiti / atredamabhidhīte - sādhanaṃ khalu sarvatra sādhyasādhanayoḥ sarvopasaṃhareṇa pramāṇena vyāptau siddhāyāṃ sādhyaṃ gamayediti sarvavādisammatam / tatra yadi dṛsyaśarīraviśiṣṭena buddhimatā vyāptirgṛhyate tadā tathābhūtasādhyamantareṇāpi jāyamāne tṛṇādau kāryatvasya darśanāt prameyatvādivat sādhāraṇānaikāntiko 'yaṃ hetuḥ / tṛṇādayaḥ pakṣīkṛtā ityapi na vaktavyam / na hi vyabhicāraviṣaya eva pakṣo bhavitumarhati-
body.translated_text: If that [effect] could exist even without an intelligent being, then it would never arise from an intelligent being either, since an effect cannot arise even once in the absence of its cause. Therefore, this should not be suspected anywhere—that something could be an effect yet not have an intelligent cause. Here it is said: it is agreed by all disputants that a means of proof (sādhana) can establish the property to be proven (sādhya) everywhere only when pervasion (vyāpti) is established by a pramāṇa (valid means of cognition) through universal correlation of the sādhya and sādhana. Now, if pervasion is established with a visible-bodied intelligent being, then since the property of being an effect (kāryatva) is observed even in grass and the like that arise without such an agent—just like the property of being a knowable (prameyatva)—this reason becomes an inconclusive common reason (<s>sādhāraṇa-anaikāntika</s>). Nor should it be said that grass and the like are included in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), for the very locus of deviation cannot properly be the subject—

body.text: `sandigdhe hetuvacanāt vyasto hetoranāśraya' iti nyāyāt /
body.translated_text: 'When the reason is stated in a doubtful case, the thesis is overturned and the reason lacks a basis'—according to this principle.

body.text: athāśakyārohaṇe 'pi parvate dahanamantareṇa ca dhūmadarśanāt, evaṃ dhūme 'pi vyabhicāro vaktuṃ sulabha eva? tanna / aśakyārohaṇatvena parvate dahanasya draṣṭumaśakyatvāt yuktaṃ tatra sandigdhaviṣayatvam / prastute tu dṛśyaśarīraviśiṣṭena buddhimatā vyāptau gṛhyamāṇāyāṃ dṛśyānupalambhena buddhimato bādho bhavatīti yuktam / atha dṛśyaśarīreṇa buddhimanmātreṇa vā vyāptiravagamyate tadā adṛśyasya buddhimanmātrasya vā sādhyasya dṛśyānupalambhena vyatirekāsiddheḥ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttiko 'yaṃ hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: But [objection:] even on an inaccessible mountain, smoke is seen without fire—so could not deviation be easily stated for smoke as well? No. Because the mountain is inaccessible, fire cannot be seen there, so doubt in that case is justified. But in the present case, when pervasion is established with a visible-bodied intelligent being, the intelligent being is refuted by the non-apprehension of what is perceptible (<s>dṛśya-anupalambha</s>)—this is proper. Now if pervasion is understood with a visible body or with a mere intelligent being [including supersensory ones], then since the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) cannot be established through the non-apprehension of a supersensory being or of a mere intelligent being as <s>sādhya</s>, this reason has doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar case (<s>sandigdha-vipakṣa-vyāvṛttika</s>).

body.text: sādhyābhāvaprayuktasya sādhānābhāvasya [kāśadāva] siddhatvena vyāpterabhāvāt tathā coktam jñānaśrīmitrapādaiḥ / kāryatvasya vipakṣavṛttihataye sambhāvyate 'tīndriyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because there is no pervasion, given that the absence of the means of proof entailed by the absence of the property to be proven is [not] established [in cases like space]. Thus <s>Jñānaśrīmitrapāda</s> has stated: 'In order to defeat the presence of the property of being an effect in the dissimilar case, a supersensory

body.text: kartā cedvayatirekasiddhividhurā vyāptiḥ kathaṃ sidhyati //
body.translated_text: creator is postulated. But if so, how can pervasion, bereft of the establishment of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), be proven?'

children.translated_text: 'If, on the other hand, a visible creator is relied upon so that the establishment of negative concomitance may be achieved,
then grass and the like clearly constitute observation of the dissimilar case.'

body.text: trilocanābhyupagatasya vahnidhūmayoḥ svābhāvavika sambandhavādasya nirasanam
body.translated_text: Refutation of the doctrine of natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) connection between fire and smoke, as accepted by <s>Trilocana</s>

body.text: yacca trilocanenoktam-
body.translated_text: And what <s>Trilocana</s> has said—

body.text:
`yathā svābhāvikaḥ sambandho dhūmādīnāṃ vahnayādibhissaha tathā
kāryatvasya buddhimatā sārdham, tadupādheranupalabhyamānatvāt,
kvacidvyabhicārasyādarśanāt' iti /
body.translated_text: 'Just as there is a natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) connection of smoke and the like with fire and the like, so too [there is a natural connection] of the property of being an effect with an intelligent being, because no limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) for it is apprehended, and because deviation is nowhere observed'—

body.text: tanna yuktam / yato 'rthāntaraṃ kiñcidapekṣaṇīyamupādhiśabdenābhidhīyate / na cārthāntaramavaśyaṃ dṛśyaṃ syāt / adṛśyamapi deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛsṭam sambhāvyate / ato dhūmasya dahanena saha sambandhe bhaviṣyatyupādhiḥ / na copalabhyata iti kathamadarśanamātreṇa nāstyevetyucyate / yadapyuktaṃ vyabhicārasyādarśanāditi sādhanaṃ, tadapi sandigdhāsiddham / pratyayāntaravaikalyenāhatya vyabhicārasyādarśane 'pi sarvatra niṣeddhumaśakyatvāt / na caitāvatā prāmaṇikalokayātrātikramaḥ / prāmāṇikaireva sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāve saṃśayasya vihitatvāt / na ca caivaṃ saṃśayena sarvatrapravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ, pramāṇādarthasandehācca pravṛtterupapatteḥ / yadapyuktam -
body.translated_text: that is not valid. Because something additional that needs to be considered is denoted by the word <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition). And that additional factor need not necessarily be visible; even what is invisible, being remote in space, time, and nature, is conceivable. Therefore, in the connection of smoke with fire too, there may be a limiting condition. And since it is not apprehended, how can one say merely from non-observation that it absolutely does not exist? As for the statement that 'deviation is not observed' being offered as proof—that too is of doubtful establishment (<s>sandigdha-asiddha</s>), because even when deviation is not observed due to the incompleteness of other conditions, it cannot be universally negated. Nor does this transgress the conduct of those who rely on valid means of cognition. For those very authorities prescribe doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) in the absence of both establishing and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s>. Nor would there be the absurd consequence of action everywhere based on doubt, because action proceeds from the ascertainment of an object through a <s>pramāṇa</s> or from doubt about an object. And what has been stated—

body.text: `yathānyatvāviśeṣe 'pi bauddhānāṃ kiñcideva vastu kāryaṃ syāt,
body.translated_text: 'Just as for the Buddhists, even though there is no distinction of otherness, only certain things are effects

body.text: kiñcideva kāraṇaṃ, na sarva, tathā mamāpyanyatvāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcideva
body.translated_text: and only certain things are causes, not everything; so too for me, even though there is no distinction of otherness, only certain

body.text: dhūmādikaṃ vastu svābhāvika sambandhena sambaddhaṃ na sarvam' iti /
body.translated_text: things like smoke are connected by a natural relation, not everything'—

body.text: tanna yuktam / yathā dhūmākhyaṃ vastu dahanāyattamiti pramāṇasiddhiṃ tathā kiṃ svābhāvikasambandho 'pi pramāṇasiddhaḥ, yenaivamucyate? kiñca svābhāvikasambandha iti ko 'rthaḥ? kiṃ svato bhūtaḥ, svahetorvā bhūtaḥ ahetuko vā iti trayo vikalpāḥ / tatra na tāvadādyaḥ pakṣaḥ, svātmani kriyāvirodhāt / nāpi dvitīyaḥ, tadutpattisambandhasvīkāraprasaṅgāt / athāhetukaḥ, tadā deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvādatīvāsaṅgataḥ svābhāvikasambandhavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: that is not valid. Just as the fact that smoke depends on fire is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, is the natural connection also established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that one can speak thus? Moreover, what is the meaning of 'natural connection' (<s>svābhāvika-sambandha</s>)? Three alternatives arise: is it self-produced, produced from its own cause, or causeless? The first alternative is untenable, because action upon oneself is contradictory. Nor the second, because that would amount to accepting the connection of origination (<s>tadutpatti-sambandha</s>). If it is causeless, then due to the absence of restriction by place, time, and nature, the doctrine of natural connection is utterly incoherent.

body.text: kiñca sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa vā dṛṣṭāntamātramastīti na vyāptisiddhiḥ / yadṛcchayā militayorapi karabhagadarbhayostathābhāvaprasaṅgāt / tasmānnidarśanaṃ nāma [dṛṣṭānta ucyate / sa ca] gṛhītavismṛtapratibandhasādhaka pramāṇasmaraṇadvāreṇaiva hetāvupayujyate, na svasannidhimātreṇa / tathāhi - na tāvadākāśe sādhyābhāvena sadhanābhāvaḥ pratīyate / ākāśe hi yathā buddhimatkāraṇanivṛttistathā acetanasyāpi kāraṇasya nivṛttirnāstyeva / tatkasyābhāvaprayuktakāryatvābhāvaḥ pratīyatāṃ, yena sādhyābhāvaprayuktasādhanābhāva vyatirekaḥ sidhyatīti / nāpi ghaṭe kāryatvasya buddhimadanvayadarśanādākāśe 'pi buddhimadabhāvādeva kāryatvābhāvo vaktuṃ yujyate, yasmādanayostādātmyaṃ tadutpattiranyo vā svābhāvikādisambandhaḥ pūrvapramāṇena na prasādhitaḥ syādityuktam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the mere existence of an example through similarity or dissimilarity does not establish pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), because of the absurd consequence that even a camel and <s>darbha</s> grass that meet by chance would have such a relation. Therefore, what is called an illustration [is an example]. And it [the example] is useful for the reason only through the door of recollecting the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the connection which was grasped and forgotten—not by its mere presence. For: in space, the absence of the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) is not perceived through the absence of the property to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>). In space, just as the cessation of an intelligent cause occurs, so too the cessation of a non-intelligent cause occurs—it is not that only [the intelligent cause ceases]. Then whose absence-entailed absence of being-an-effect is to be perceived, by which the negative concomitance—the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> entailed by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>—would be established? Nor is it proper to say that because in a pot, the property of being an effect is seen together with an intelligent being, therefore in space too, the absence of being-an-effect follows simply from the absence of an intelligent being—because neither identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), nor origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>), nor any other natural connection between these has been established by any prior <s>pramāṇa</s>—as has been stated.

body.text: adarśanamātreṇa vyatireko 'siddhaḥ
body.translated_text: Non-establishment of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) by mere non-observation

body.text: kiñcādarśanamātrena vyatireko na sidhyati / tathā hi, vipakṣe heturnopalabhyata ityanena tadupalambhakapramāṇa nivṛttirucyate / pramāṇaṃ ca prameyasya kāryam, 'nākāraṇaṃ viṣaya' iti nyāyāt / na ca kāryanivṛttau kāraṇanivṛttiryujyate, nirdhūmasyāpi vahnerbhānāt / yadi punaḥ pramāṇasattayā prameyasattā vyāptā syāt, tadā yuktamevaitat / kevalamiyameva vyāptirasambhāvinī, sarvasya sarvadarśitvaprasaṅgāt / tasmānnādarśanamātreṇa vyatirekaḥ sidhyati / yathoktam - 'sarvādṛṣṭiśca sandigdhā svādṛṣṭirvyabhicāriṇī /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, negative concomitance is not established by mere non-observation. For: 'the reason is not apprehended in the dissimilar case' means the cessation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that apprehends it. And the <s>pramāṇa</s> is the effect of the knowable object (<s>prameya</s>), according to the principle: 'the object is not without being a cause [of cognition].' And it is not proper that the cessation of a cause follows from the cessation of an effect, since fire exists even without smoke. If, however, the existence of the knowable were pervaded by the existence of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then this would indeed be valid. But this very pervasion is impossible, because of the absurd consequence that everyone would be omniscient. Therefore, negative concomitance is not established by mere non-observation. As stated: 'All non-observation is doubtful; one's own non-observation deviates,

body.text: bhūjalāntargatasyāpi bījasyāsattvadarśanāt' // iti //
body.translated_text: because even of a seed inside water in the earth, its non-existence is observed.'

body.text: vācaspatimatanirasanam
body.translated_text: Refutation of the position of <s>Vācaspati</s> (<s>Miśra</s>)

body.text: yadapi vācaspatirāha -
body.translated_text: And what <s>Vācaspati</s> has said—

body.text: `viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣa eva saṃśayo bhavati tato yathādarśanameva śaṅkitumucitam' iti /
body.translated_text: 'Doubt arises only when a particular recollection is relevant; therefore, it is proper to doubt only in accordance with what is observed'—

body.text:
atrocyate - nāyaṃ nyāyaḥ sārvatrikaḥ / tathā cābhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ /
tathā hi - [kāryatvadhūmatvayoḥ] tādātmyatadutpattisambandha viyogitvena sādhāraṇena dharmeṇa prameyatvadhūmatvakāryatvādīnāṃ tanmatenāpi sajātīyatvam / tatra prameyatvasyavyabhicāradarśanamevānyatrāpi śaṅkāmupasthāpayatīti yathādarśanamevedamāśaṅkitam / ataḥ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvaṃ nāma hetudūṣaṇaṃ durvārameva / etacca saddūṣaṇameva /
ato yadanenoktam - 'nāyaṃ hetudoṣaḥ, ato na parihartavyaḥ, tasya copanyāso 'doṣodbhāvanaṃ nāma nigrahasthānam' iti / tadidānīṃ svamatenaivānena vādinā niranuyojyānuyogalakṣaṇena nigrahasthānenātmā bādhita ityupekṣaṇiyo 'yaṃ devānāṃ priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: to this we reply: this principle is not universal. And even conceding it, we say: since the properties of being-an-effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), being-smoke (<s>dhūmatva</s>), being-knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>), and the like are of the same class by virtue of lacking the connections of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>)—this being so even according to his own doctrine—the observation of the non-deviation of being-knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>) elsewhere brings up the suspicion here too. Thus this has been doubted in accordance with what is observed. Therefore, the fault of having doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar case (<s>sandigdha-vipakṣa-vyāvṛttitva</s>) is indeed irremediable. And this is a genuine fault. Therefore, what he has said—'This is not a fault of the reason; hence it need not be addressed; and its presentation constitutes the defeat-point (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) called attributing a fault where none exists'—now, by his own doctrine, this disputant has struck himself with the <s>nigrahasthāna</s> characterized as objecting to one who is not to be objected to. This dear friend of the gods should be disregarded.

body.text: īśvarasādhakānumāne anupapattiḥ
body.translated_text: The impossibility in the inference proving <s>Īśvara</s> (God)

body.text: nanu yadi dṛśyāgnidhūmasāmānyayoriva dṛśyātmanoreva kāryakāraṇasāmānyayoḥ pratyakṣānulambhato vyāptistadā santānāntarānumānaṃ na syāt, paracittasyādṛśyātmakatayā vyāptigrahaṇakāle 'nantarbhāvāditi cet? na / svasaṃvedanaṃ hi tatra vyāptigrāhakam / svasaṃvedanamātrāpekṣayā paricittasyāpi dṛśyatvāt / na caivaṃ vyāvahārikendriyapratyakṣamātrabuddhimanmātraṃ jaṭharacitrasādhāraṇaṃ vahnimātraṃ vā gocaro yujyate, yenāsyāpi dṛśyatā syāt / tasmāt dṛśyenaiva vahninā dhūmasya pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāptiriti nyāyaḥ // kiñca yadi buddhimanmātrapūrvakatvamanena sādhyate, tadā siddhasādhanatādūṣaṇaṃ sādhanasya / atha eko nityaḥ sarvajña ityādiviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭabuddhimatpūrvakatvaṃ sādhyate, tadā evaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭena sādhyena saha kāryatvasya sādhanasya dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi pramāṇena vyāpterasiddheranaikāntikatvam / atha sāmānyena vyāptimādāya viśeṣasya pakṣadharmatābalāt siddhirucyate? tanna yuktam / yena sādhyagatena viśeṣaṇena vinā hetorvṛttirdharmiṇi na ghaṭate, tasya viśeṣasya pakṣadharmabalādyuktā siddhiḥ / yathā dhūmāt parvatadeśavṛttitvasya dahanadharmasya, na tu tārṇatvādīnāṃ viśeṣāṇām / tārṇatāmantareṇāpi parvate dhūmadarśanāt / tadvad buddhimato 'pi śarīrādivṛttitvaṃ yadi sidhyati, siddhyatu / na punaratyantavilakṣaṇaṃ sarvajñatvam / asarvajñatve 'pi kāryatvasya sambhavāt / upādānādyabhijñatvādapi na sarvajñatvasiddhiḥ, ekatvasiddhau sidhtyetat / na caikatvaṃ siddham / anekakartṛpūrvakatve 'pi kāryatvasya sambhavāt / yathānekakīṭikāniṣpāditaḥ śakramūrdhā / atha śakramūrdhno 'pīśvarapūrvakatvaṃ sādhyaṃ, tarhi ghaṭasyāpīśvarapūrvakatvasiddhau kuto dṛṣṭāntatvam? atha kumbhakārasya kartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kathamapākriyate? kīṭakādīnāṃ ca hetutvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tadapi kathaṃ vāryate? nāpi bahūnāṃ kāraṇatve vipratipattisambhāvanā, dṛṣṭatvādeveti / tasmāt sādhyasādhanayoḥ sarvopasaṃhāravatī vyāptirdṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi pramāṇenāvaśyaṃ darśayitavyeti sthitam / kiñca nityaikasarvajñe buddhimati sādhye viruddho 'pyeṣaḥ / anityānekāsarvajñena buddhimatā vyāptatvāt kāryatvasya / tathā hi, sādhyaviparyayasādhanādiha viruddha ucyate / ayaṃ ca sādhyaviparītaṃ sādhyatītyāstāṃ tāvat prastāvāyāteśvaradūṣaṇodbhāvanānibandhakaraṇam //
body.translated_text: Objection: If concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) is grasped only from the perceptual apprehension and non-apprehension of perceptible things — as with the universal pair of visible fire and smoke — then inference of another's mental continuum would be impossible, since another's mind, being imperceptible, would not be included at the time of grasping concomitance. Reply: No — for there, self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) is the means of grasping concomitance, since even another's mind is perceptible with respect to self-awareness alone. It is not the case that mere conventional sense-perception, or a mere intelligent [agent], or a mere fire common to stomachs and paintings, etc. is the object [required], such that [God] too would be perceptible. Therefore, the rule is that concomitance is [grasped] through perceptual apprehension and non-apprehension of the visible fire and smoke alone. Furthermore, if mere creation by an intelligent being is what is to be proved by this [argument], then the proof has the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). If, however, creation by an intelligent being qualified by [being] one, eternal, omniscient, etc. is to be proved, then the proof 'being an effect' is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since the concomitance of the proof with such a qualified probandum is not established by any <s>pramāṇa</s> in the example. Or is it said that, taking the concomitance with the general [property], the particular is established by force of the property of the subject? That is not correct. The establishment of a particular through force of the property of the subject is justified [only] when the reason cannot occur in the subject without that qualifier belonging to the probandum — as the property of fire, occurring at the mountain-location, is established from smoke; but not particular features such as being fueled by straw, etc. — since smoke is observed on the mountain even without straw-fuel. Likewise, even if the fact of an intelligent agent being located in bodies, etc. is established, let it be established. But not omniscience, which is utterly different. Since the property of being an effect is possible even without omniscience. Nor does omniscience follow from knowledge of material causes, etc. — that would follow only if oneness were established. But oneness is not established, since the property of being an effect is possible even with prior creation by multiple agents — like an anthill built by many ants. If the anthill too is claimed to have been preceded by God, then, once God's creation of the pot is to be proved, how can the pot serve as an example? Moreover, the potter's role as maker has been observed — how can that be dismissed? And the causality of ants, etc. has been observed — how can that too be denied? Nor is there any possibility of disagreement about the causality of many [agents], since it is directly observed. Therefore it is established that the complete concomitance of the probandum and the proof must necessarily be demonstrated by a <s>pramāṇa</s> in the example. Furthermore, when the probandum is an intelligent [creator] who is eternal, one, and omniscient, this [reason of 'being an effect'] is actually contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since the property of being an effect is pervaded by an intelligent agent that is non-eternal, multiple, and non-omniscient. For here, what proves the opposite of the probandum is called contradictory. And since this [reason] proves the opposite of the probandum — let us set aside [further] elaboration of the refutation of God, which has been composed incidentally.

body.text: sādharmyavaidharmyaprayogeṣu trairūpyāsiddhyāśaṃṅkā tannirasanañca
body.translated_text: Doubt about establishing the triple character (<s>trairūpya</s>) in the applications based on similarity and dissimilarity, and its resolution

body.text: nanu sādharmyavati sādhanavākye anvaya evoktaḥ na tu vyatirekaḥ / vaidharmyavati ca vyatireka evoktaḥ, na tvanvayaḥ / tatkathamābhyāṃ trirūpaṃ liṅgaṃ kathyata iti cet, naiṣa doṣaḥ / yasmāt sādharmyavati ca sādhanavākye, upanyaste sāmarthyādeva vyatireko 'vagamyate / vyatirekāgṛhītau ca sādhyābhāve 'pi na sādhanābhāva iti viparyayaḥ sambhāvayitavyaḥ / evaṃ cānvayasyaivābhāvaḥ syāt / satyapi sādhane sādhyābhāvāditi sāmarthyam / tathā vaidharmyavati sādhanavākye upanyaste sāmarthyādevānvayo 'vagamyate, anvayagṛhītau hi sādhanaṃ ca syāt sādhyaṃ ca na bhavediti viparyayaḥ sambhāvayitavyaḥ / evaṃ ca vyatireka eva na bhavet / sādhyābhāve 'pi sādhanasya bhāvāditi sāmarthyam / tasmāt dvāvapi prayogau trirūpaliṅgaprakāśakāvityadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection: In a probative statement based on similarity, only positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is stated, not negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). And in one based on dissimilarity, only negative concomitance is stated, not positive. Then how can the triple-characterized mark be expressed by these two? Reply: This is no fault. For when the probative statement based on similarity is presented, the negative concomitance is understood through the force of implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>) alone. If the negative concomitance were not grasped, then even in the absence of the probandum, the absence of the proof would not [follow] — the converse would have to be entertained. And thus there would be an absence of positive concomitance itself — since even though the proof is present, the probandum would be absent. This is the force [of implication]. Likewise, when the probative statement based on dissimilarity is presented, the positive concomitance is understood through the force of implication alone. For if the positive concomitance were not grasped, the proof would exist and yet the probandum would not — this converse would have to be entertained. And thus the negative concomitance itself would not hold — since even in the absence of the probandum, the proof would be present. This is the force [of implication]. Therefore, both applications are revealers of the triple-characterized mark — there is no fault.

body.text: vyaptigrāhaka pramāṇanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that grasps concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>)

body.text: samprati sādhyasādhanayorvyāptiḥ yatra dharmiṇi grahītavyā,yena ca pramāṇena, tadubhayaṃ sukhāvabodhārtha kathyate - svabhāvahetoḥ sattvalakṣaṇasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiḥ sādhyadharmiṇyeva grahītavyeti kecit / teṣāmantarvyāptipakṣo 'bhimataḥ / prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayābhyāṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi ghaṭādau vyāptirgrahītavyetyanye / teṣāṃ bahirvyāptipakṣo 'bhimataḥ / sattvādanyeṣāṃ svabhāvahetūnāṃ kāryahetūnāmanupalambhahetūnāṃ ca dṛṣṭānta eva vyāptirgrahītavyā / tatra śiṃśipātvasya vṛkṣatvavyavahāre, sādhye dṛṣṭānte pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāptirgrāhyā / sattvakṣaṇikatvayostu prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayābhyāṃ pramāṇābhyāṃ, sādhyaviparyayabādhakapramāṇena vā kramayaugapadyanivṛttilakṣaṇena svasaṃvedanasāmarthyasiddhervikalpasiddhervā vastutvāvastutvābhyāṃ sandihyamāne vipakṣe dharmiṇi, kāryahetordhūmādervahnyādinā mahānasādau dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi trividhapratyakṣānupalambhataḥ, pañcavidhapratyakṣānupalambhato vā vyāptirgrahītavyā / , anupalambhasya tu asadvyavahārayogyatvena saha vyāptiḥ pratyakṣeṇaiva / , anyeṣāṃ tu svabhāvahetūnāṃ kāryahetūnāṃ vā keṣāñcit, yathāsvabhāvaṃ pramāṇenonnīya grahītavyeti //
body.translated_text: Now, where the concomitance of the probandum and the proof is to be grasped — on which subject (<s>dharmin</s>) — and by which <s>pramāṇa</s>: both of these are stated for ease of understanding. Some hold that the concomitance of the essential-nature reason characterized by existence (<s>sattva</s>) with momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) is to be grasped on the subject of the probandum itself. Theirs is the position of internal concomitance (<s>antarvyāpti</s>). Others hold that the concomitance is to be grasped on the example, such as a pot, etc., through <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (converse of the reductio). Theirs is the position of external concomitance (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>). For essential-nature reasons other than existence, for effect-reasons, and for non-apprehension reasons, the concomitance is to be grasped in the example itself. There, for the being-a-<s>śiṃśapā</s>-tree in the conventional usage of being-a-tree: the concomitance on the probandum and the example is to be grasped through perceptual apprehension and non-apprehension. But for existence and momentariness, [the concomitance is to be grasped] through the two <s>pramāṇas</s> of <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s>, or through the <s>pramāṇa</s> that invalidates the opposite of the probandum — characterized by the elimination of sequence and simultaneity — through the power of self-awareness or through conceptual establishment, when the counter-example subject is doubtful between being real and unreal. For the effect-reason such as smoke with fire, on the example-subject such as a kitchen: concomitance is to be grasped from three types of perceptual apprehension and non-apprehension, or from five types. For non-apprehension, the concomitance with fitness for the conventional usage of non-existence is [grasped] through perception alone. For other essential-nature reasons and some effect-reasons, it is to be ascertained by the appropriate <s>pramāṇa</s> according to their respective natures.

body.text: hetvābhāsanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Examination of fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>)

body.text: vyāptyaniścaye hetoranaikāntiko doṣaḥ / sa ca trividhaḥ - asādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ, sandhigdhavipakṣavyāāvṛttikaśceti / tatra asādhāraṇānaikāntiko yathā - sātmakaṃ jīvaccharīram, prāṇādimattvāt aparajīvaccharīravat, ghaṭavat / ayaṃ heturaparajīvaccharīre ātmanā vyāpta iti na niścitaḥ / ghaṭe ca vipakṣe ātmano 'bhāvānnivṛtta iti na niścitaḥ / dharmiṇi tu jīvaccharīre vidyata iti asādhāraṇānaikāntika ucyate / aparaścāsādhāraṇo yathā - anityaśabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt, ghaṭavat, ākāśavaditi / sādhāraṇanaikāntiko yathā - nityaḥ śabdaḥ prameyatvāt, ghaṭavat ākāśavat / , sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttiko yathā - saḥ śyāmastatputratvāt, paridṛśyamānatatputravaditi //
body.translated_text: When concomitance is not ascertained, the fault of the reason is inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>). And that is threefold: uncommon inconclusive (<s>asādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), common inconclusive (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), and doubtful exclusion from the counter-example (<s>sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttika</s>). Among these, an example of the uncommon inconclusive: 'A living body possesses a self (<s>ātman</s>), because it possesses life-breath, etc. — like another living body, like a pot.' This reason is not ascertained to be pervaded by the self in another living body. Nor is it ascertained to be excluded in the pot, the counter-example, because of the absence of the self. But it exists in the subject, the living body — therefore it is called uncommon inconclusive. Another uncommon example: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being audible — like a pot, like space.' An example of the common inconclusive: 'Sound is eternal, because of being knowable — like a pot, like space.' An example of doubtful exclusion from the counter-example: 'He is dark, because he is a son of that [father] — like the observed son of that [father].'

body.text: yaduktaṃ prāk, sattvasya kṣaṇikatvena saha vyāptiḥ prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparpayābhyāṃ grahītavyeti, tatra ko 'yaṃ prasaṅgo nāma? pramāṇaprasiddhavyāptikena vākyena parasyāniṣṭatvāpādanāya prasañjanam prasaṅgaḥ, yathā - sāmānyasya, anekavṛttitvābhyupagame anekatvaprasañjanam / tathā hi - yadanekavṛtti tadanekaṃ yathā anekabhājanagataṃ tālapham / anekavṛtti ca sāmānyam / tasmādanenāpyanekena bhavitavyamiti prasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: As was stated earlier, the concomitance of existence with momentariness is to be grasped through <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s>. What then is this <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio)? <s>Prasaṅga</s> is the consequence-deduction (<s>prasañjana</s>) aimed at attributing something undesired to the opponent, by means of a statement whose concomitance is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
